guidelines.screenSubtitle: Prevention, symptoms, and care - all in one place.
guidelines.disclaimer: This guide is general public-health information, not medical advice. Always follow your doctor's instructions.

mosquito.title: The Aedes Mosquito
mosquito.intro: Knowing the mosquito that spreads dengue is the first step to avoiding it.
bullets: The Aedes mosquito usually bites during the day - especially in the early morning and late afternoon - not just at night.
It has distinctive black-and-white stripes on its body and legs.
It breeds in small amounts of clean, still water - buckets, flower pots, gutters, discarded tyres, and water-storage containers.
Eggs can hatch in water that has been sitting for less than a week, so containers need emptying or covering often.
It doesn't travel far from where it hatches, so one infected home is often the source for the whole street.

prevention.title: Preventing Dengue
prevention.intro: Protect yourself and stop the mosquito from breeding around you.
bullets: Use mosquito repellent on exposed skin, especially during the day.
Wear long sleeves and long trousers where practical, especially at dawn and dusk.
Fit mosquito nets or screens on windows, doors, and beds.
Use a mosquito coil or plug-in repellent indoors, especially in shaded rooms.
Empty, scrub, or cover anything that can hold still water around your home at least once a week.
Support fogging and inspection visits from your local health authority.

symptoms.title: Recognizing Symptoms
symptoms.intro: Dengue symptoms usually start 4-10 days after being bitten.
bullets: Sudden high fever, often 39-40°C.
Severe headache and pain behind the eyes.
Muscle, joint, and bone pain - sometimes called "breakbone fever".
Nausea, vomiting, and loss of appetite.
A skin rash that can appear a few days after the fever starts.
Mild bleeding - nosebleeds, bleeding gums, or easy bruising.

careSteps.title: If You Suspect Dengue
careSteps.intro: What to do from the very first day of fever.
bullets: See a doctor promptly for a blood test to confirm the diagnosis.
Rest as much as possible and avoid strenuous activity.
Drink plenty of fluids to prevent dehydration - track your intake in the Fluids tab.
Use paracetamol only for fever and pain. Never take aspirin, ibuprofen, diclofenac, or other NSAIDs - they raise the risk of bleeding.
Log your temperature and symptoms daily in this app so changes are easy to spot.
Watch closely for warning signs, especially from day 3 onward as the fever starts to settle.

diet.title: Food & Drinks Guide
diet.intro: What to eat and drink - and what to avoid - while recovering.
preferBullets: Water, ORS/Jeevani, king coconut water, and clear soups to stay hydrated.
Soft, easy-to-digest foods - porridge, rice with soup, mashed vegetables.
Fruits rich in vitamin C, such as oranges and papaya, to support recovery.
avoidBullets: Dark or red-coloured drinks - beetroot, blackcurrant, and grape juice can look like blood if you vomit or pass blood.
Alcohol and caffeinated drinks - both can worsen dehydration.
Oily, spicy, or fried food, which can be harder to digest while unwell.
Aspirin, ibuprofen, diclofenac, mefenamic acid, and other NSAIDs - paracetamol only.

warningSigns.title: Emergency Warning Signs
warningSigns.intro: If you or someone you're caring for has any of these signs, go to a hospital immediately - do not wait.

community.title: Community Prevention
community.intro: Dengue control works best as a shared effort.
bullets: Empty, scrub, cover, or dispose of containers that collect water at least once a week.
Get rid of unused tyres, bottles, cans, and other rubbish that can collect rainwater.
Clean roof gutters and drains so water can't pool.
Cover water-storage tanks and barrels tightly.
Report mosquito breeding sites in your area to your local health authority.
